conventions.tracks: snapshot = steps 24, 34, 37, 38 only (placed-orders-24mo.json is written by step 38). deep = all steps (24, 31, 34, 35, 37, 38, 40, 29), v2 event exports/censuses, and manual verification.
conventions.paths: Paths are relative to klaviyo-audit/output/<slug>/<file>. [] marks an array. Step 38 monthly aggregates live at aggregates.<key>.current|prior.{dates[], rows[].dimensions[], rows[].measurements.<count|sum_value|unique>[]}; windows.current is the account-local Nov-1-to-capture window and windows.prior the 12 months before it.
conventions.flow_classifier: Used by every FLW/RET presence check. A flow is a LIVE flow of type X when (a) flows.items[].attributes.status == 'live' and archived == false; (b) its trigger flows.details[].definition.triggers[0] maps to X: type 'list' or metric 'Subscribed to Email Marketing'/'Subscribed to List'/form-submit -> welcome; metric 'Started Checkout'/'Checkout Started' -> abandoned_checkout; 'Added to Cart' -> abandoned_cart; 'Viewed Product' -> browse; 'Placed Order'/'Fulfilled Order'/'Ordered Product' -> post_purchase (or replenishment/winback when the first send waits >= 21 / >= 45 days or the name says so); trigger type 'segment' -> sunset or winback by segment definition; subscription-platform metrics -> subscription; 'Subscribed to Back in Stock' -> back_in_stock. Join metric triggers via triggers[0].id -> metrics.items[].id -> attributes.name and attributes.integration.name. Custom API metrics (e.g. names like revamp_abandoned_checkout) and name-only matches must be confirmed by a human; (c) it has >= 1 send-email or send-sms action in flows.details[].definition.actions[] with data.status == 'live'; (d) performance-cross-review.json reports.flow90...results[] shows recipients > 0 for that flow_id. Message count = live send actions on the main path.
conventions.na_rule: A check whose precondition is absent (no SMS program, no subscription product, no Klaviyo SMS) is scored 'n/a', never pass and never fail. A missing metric or zero series is 'unknown' until DAT checks clear it; unavailable data is never a measured zero.
conventions.privacy: Checks operate on aggregates and pseudonymous profile IDs only. Never copy emails, names, phones, addresses or raw profile IDs into findings.

areas.label: Data integrity & source
areas.description: Is the commerce and engagement data we score from complete, canonical, timezone-correct and reconcilable? Every other area depends on these passing.

areas.label: List growth & forms
areas.description: Are new subscribers being captured, converted by forms, and routed into the welcome journey?

areas.label: Core automation coverage & health
areas.description: Are the revenue-critical flows live, sending, filtered correctly and earning their share?

areas.label: Campaigns
areas.description: Is campaign cadence, targeting and revenue per recipient healthy and safe?

areas.label: Deliverability
areas.description: Do emails reach the inbox: complaint, bounce and unsubscribe rates, provider-level engagement, and authenticated sending.

areas.label: Repeat purchase, subscription & winback
areas.description: Do first-time buyers come back, on what timing, and is subscription lifecycle data and messaging working?

areas.label: Rendering, clipping, links & offers
areas.description: Does the message the customer receives render, track, link and honour its offer?

areas.label: SMS
areas.description: Is SMS consent captured, compliant, measured and reconciled with any third-party SMS platform?

checks.title: One canonical order source is selected
checks.question: Is revenue being read from the store's real, active Placed Order metric rather than a dormant or duplicate integration?
checks.why_it_matters: If we read revenue from the wrong or a dormant integration, every revenue number in the audit is wrong.

source.path: 38: metricChoices.placed_order.used{id,name,integration}, metricChoices.placed_order.otherCandidates[], aggregates.placed_order.current.rows[0].measurements.count[]; 34: placedOrderCandidates[].integration.name, conversionMetric.id; deep: v2 source-contract.json metricIds['Placed Order'], excluded{}.events_2024-10-01_to_asof

checks.logic: List every Placed Order candidate. For each, get events in the last 90 days (deep: source-contract.json event counts; snapshot: the used metric's last 3 monthly counts, others flagged for review). Pass if the used metric holds >= 95% of last-90-day Placed Order events, matches the store platform the client confirms, and step 34 conversionMetric.id == step 38 metricChoices.placed_order.used.id. Warn if other candidates have recent events (5-20% share) or the platform is unconfirmed. Fail if the used metric has < 80% share, has zero events in the latest full month, or steps 34 and 38 used different metrics.

thresholds.pass: used metric >= 95% of last-90-day order events and same metric in steps 34 and 38
thresholds.warn: competing candidate with 5-20% of recent events, or store platform unconfirmed
thresholds.fail: used metric < 80% share, zero events in latest full month, or steps disagree

impact.method: Not sized directly; a fail blocks all revenue-sized findings until rerun with the corrected metric.

checks.fix: Pin the canonical Placed Order metric ID in the audit config (as v2 source-contract.json does), rerun steps 34/35/38 with it, and record excluded candidates with their event counts.
checks.notes: Lesson: WooCommerce stores carried dormant Shopify Placed Order metrics; an earlier audit used the wrong funnel metric source.

checks.title: Flow triggers listen to live, canonical events
checks.question: Does each live flow trigger on a metric that is actually receiving events from the current store integration?
checks.why_it_matters: A flow wired to a dead or duplicate event looks live in Klaviyo but never sends to anyone.
checks.logic: For each live flow with a metric trigger, resolve triggers[0].id to its metric name and integration. Compare with the step 38 metric chosen for that event (metricChoices.<event>.used.id). Pass if every live flow triggers on the canonical metric and that metric had events in the latest full month. Warn if a live flow triggers on a custom API metric (needs a human to confirm its source) or on a non-canonical duplicate with recent events. Fail if any live flow triggers on a metric with zero events in the last two full months, or on a dormant integration of the same event name.

thresholds.pass: all live metric-triggered flows on canonical, active metrics
thresholds.warn: custom/duplicate trigger metric that still has events
thresholds.fail: >= 1 live flow on a metric with zero events in the last 2 full months

impact.method: For each broken trigger, size as the corresponding FLW check would size a missing flow (eligible monthly events x target recovery RPR x 12).

checks.fix: Rebuild or clone the flow onto the canonical metric (keep filters and content), test with a real event, then turn off the version on the dormant metric.
checks.notes: Also applies to profile_filter conditions of type profile-metric whose metric_id points at a dormant Placed Order metric.

checks.title: Order events carry line items and one currency
checks.question: Do order events include product line items and a consistent currency, so product, replenishment and value analysis is possible?
checks.why_it_matters: Without product line items we cannot target by product or time refills, and mixed currencies make order values meaningless.

source.path: orders[].i (item names, max 8), orders[].v, orders[].t; deep: v2/events/placed_order/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl.gz props.$extra.Items[].{ProductId,SKU,Quantity}, props.$currency_code

checks.logic: Share of orders in the last 12 months with a non-empty items array (orders[].i length > 0). Deep: also count distinct props.$currency_code values and the share of value not in account.currency (account-totals.json account.currency). Pass if >= 95% of orders have items and >= 99% of value is in one currency. Warn if 70-95% have items. Fail if < 70% have items or > 1% of value is in another currency without conversion.

thresholds.pass: >= 95% orders with items; >= 99% value single currency
thresholds.fail: < 70% orders with items, or > 1% value in unconverted foreign currency

impact.method: Not sized; failing blocks product-level segmentation, replenishment timing (RET-02) and catalog-based personalization.

checks.fix: First confirm the extractor reads both numeric Items objects and $extra.line_items (order-items.js); if the payload is truly empty, fix the store integration or add an Ordered Product feed, then normalise currency at ingestion.
checks.notes: Step 38 compact orders show empty i[] for both Shopify accounts on file; per the README the extractor was patched, so an empty array must be investigated before calling it a business problem. Currency is deep-only (v2 events).

checks.title: Reporting periods follow the account timezone
checks.question: Are monthly and daily buckets cut at local midnight in the account's timezone, with partial periods labelled?
checks.why_it_matters: Cutting months at UTC midnight shifts orders between months and makes month-over-month comparisons wrong.

source.path: 38: account.timezone, windows.current.{start,end}, aggregates.*.current.dates[]; 24: account.items[0].attributes.timezone; 35 (deep): timezone, monthly.*[].value.{start,end,interval}

checks.logic: Confirm step 24 and step 38 timezones match. For each date bucket, its UTC offset must equal the account timezone's offset at that local midnight (DST-aware, as aggregate-boundaries.js does). Flag the final bucket as partial when windows.current.end is before the bucket end. Pass if all buckets align and partial periods are labelled. Warn if only the partial-period label is missing. Fail if buckets are UTC-cut for a non-UTC account or timezones disagree.

thresholds.pass: all buckets at local midnight; partial period labelled
thresholds.fail: UTC-cut buckets for non-UTC account, or timezone mismatch between steps

impact.method: Not sized; affects accuracy of every period comparison.

checks.fix: Regenerate aggregates through aggregate-boundaries.js local-midnight conversion and label the in-progress month as partial in every chart.
checks.notes: Lesson: a UTC cutoff moved five orders out of one month in the first monthly pull.

checks.title: The snapshot is complete
checks.question: Did every collector call succeed without truncation, page caps or errors?
checks.why_it_matters: A silently cut-off export makes missing data look like missing marketing.

source.path: 24: {flows,campaigns,forms,lists,segments,metrics,templates}.truncated, flows.messageCapHit, *.ok, flows.details[].errors[]; 34: reports.*.ok; 38: errors[], orders.{truncated,error}, campaigns.email.truncated, catalog.truncated, coupons.truncated; 31 (deep): details[].versionErrors; 37: errors

checks.logic: Collect every truncated/capHit/ok/error flag. Pass if none are truncated or failed. Warn if only non-scoring sections failed (e.g. reports.flowSeriesWeekly365). Fail if any scoring input (flows, campaigns, orders, step 34 reports, aggregates used by a check) is truncated or errored; affected checks are scored 'unknown'.

thresholds.fail: any scoring input truncated or errored

impact.method: Not sized; gates the checks that use the affected input.

checks.fix: Rerun the failed step with --steps after fixing the cause (rate limit, page cap, request shape); record any remaining gap in the coverage page.
checks.notes: Presence/absence check. Known recurring error: step 38 flowSeriesWeekly365 fails in all four saved snapshots ('Group by flow_message_id is required').

checks.title: Attributed revenue reconciles
checks.question: Does Klaviyo-attributed revenue sit below total store revenue, and do flow revenue figures agree between reports?
checks.why_it_matters: If attribution numbers don't add up, we can't tell the client what email actually earns.
checks.logic: (1) Sum of by-channel attributed value must be <= total Placed Order value per month. (2) Sum of by-flow attributed value must be <= email-channel attributed value. (3) Attributed share = channel sum / total over the current window. (4) Step 34 flow365 conversion_value vs step 38 by-flow sum, scaled to the same months, within tolerance. Pass if (1),(2) hold, share is 10-50%, and (4) within 15%. Warn if share is 50-65% or (4) differs 15-30%. Fail if attributed exceeds total in any month, share > 65%, or (4) differs > 30%.

thresholds.fail: attributed > total in any month, share > 65%, or gap > 30%

impact.method: Not sized; a high attributed share is reported as an attribution-window issue, not a performance win.
inputs: attributed revenue by channel and flow

checks.fix: Document the attribution window and basis (event time vs send date) on the coverage page, report store revenue and attributed revenue separately, and never add channel, flow and campaign wins together.
checks.notes: Step 34 uses Klaviyo's rolling last_365_days while step 38 uses Nov-1-to-capture; align windows before comparing. Attribution window settings themselves are not in the API (manual).

checks.title: Sendable reach is measured, not list size
checks.question: How many profiles can actually be emailed or texted today after consent, suppression and overlap?
checks.why_it_matters: List and segment counts include unsubscribed and suppressed people, so they overstate how many customers we can reach.

source.path: today only: account-totals.json groupCounts.{lists,segments}[].profileCount (NOT reach); v2/list-members/<listId>.jsonl.gz rows {p,created,joined} (membership only, no consent); supplemental deep-dive/profile-reach.json (2 brands, not in runner)

checks.logic: For the main audience lists/segments, deduplicate pseudonymous profile IDs across groups, join to current email/SMS marketing consent and suppression, and report: union size, consented-and-not-suppressed size, and the ratio to raw list count. Pass if reach is measured and used in every sizing. Warn if only raw counts exist but are labelled as such. Fail if any opportunity is sized on raw list counts or summed overlapping lists.

thresholds.pass: consented, deduplicated reach measured and used
thresholds.fail: sizing uses raw or summed overlapping counts

impact.method: Not sized; reach is an input to every CAP/FLW/RET/SMS sizing.

checks.fix: Add a runner step that pages list/segment members with subscription fields, keeps aggregate counts only (pattern: 40-fetch-profile-reach.js), and write reach-census.json.
checks.notes: Lesson: list counts are not sendable reach; historical buyers are not permissioned audience.

checks.title: A sign-up popup is live and converting
checks.question: Is there a live popup or flyout, and what share of people who see it sign up?
checks.why_it_matters: The popup is usually the biggest source of new subscribers; a weak or missing one starves every flow downstream.
checks.logic: Identify live forms (status 'live'). Deep: keep form_type popup/flyout; snapshot: treat the live form with the most viewed_form_uniques as the primary capture form. Primary submit rate = submits / viewed_form_uniques over 365 days. Pass if a live popup/flyout exists with submit rate >= 3%. Warn if 1.5-3%, or only an embed form is live. Fail if no live form, or primary rate < 1.5%.

impact.method: Annual form views x (target submit rate - current) x welcome-flow revenue per new subscriber.
inputs: welcome revenue per recipient from step 34

checks.fix: Launch or rebuild a two-step popup (email, then phone) with a clear offer, exit-intent plus delay/scroll triggers, suppression of existing subscribers, and an A/B test on offer and headline.
checks.notes: Form type is only available in step 31 (deep). Submit rate counts form submits, not confirmed consent.

checks.title: The email list is growing net of unsubscribes
checks.question: Are more people subscribing to email each month than unsubscribing?
checks.why_it_matters: A shrinking list means future campaign and flow revenue is shrinking too.
checks.logic: Net growth per full month = subscribed_email uniques - unsubscribed_email uniques. Evaluate the last 3 full months and compare the current-window monthly average to the same months in the prior window. Pass if net positive in all 3 months and gross subscribes are >= 80% of the prior-year same months. Warn if net positive on average but negative in a month, or gross subscribes fell 20-50% year over year. Fail if net negative over the 3 months, or gross subscribes fell > 50%.

thresholds.pass: net positive each of last 3 months; gross >= 80% of prior year
thresholds.warn: net positive on average only, or gross down 20-50% YoY
thresholds.fail: net negative over 3 months, or gross down > 50% YoY

impact.method: Shortfall in monthly net subscribers vs prior year x 12 x average annual revenue per subscriber (email-attributed revenue / average subscriber base).

checks.fix: Restore capture (CAP-01), add checkout and account-creation consent, and investigate unsubscribe spikes by campaign (DLV-03).
checks.notes: Subscribed to Email Marketing counts consent events; list imports and suppressions can move list size without these events.

checks.title: Every live form feeds a list with a live welcome
checks.question: Does each live form add people to a list (or event) that triggers a live welcome flow?
checks.why_it_matters: If a form drops sign-ups into a list nothing listens to, new subscribers never get their welcome or promised offer.
checks.logic: For each live form, collect every list_id in its live version. Match against live flows with a list trigger of the same id (or a metric trigger on the form-submit/subscribe event). Pass if every live form maps to a live welcome flow. Warn if mapped only via a generic subscribe metric, or the list uses double opt-in and the welcome triggers before confirmation. Fail if any live form's list has no live flow trigger.

thresholds.pass: all live forms mapped to a live welcome
thresholds.warn: indirect mapping or double opt-in timing issue
thresholds.fail: >= 1 live form with no live welcome on its list

impact.method: Monthly submits from unmapped forms x welcome revenue per recipient x 12.

checks.fix: Point the form's submit action at the welcome list (or add that list as a second trigger via a list-triggered flow) and submit a test sign-up to confirm entry.
checks.notes: Presence/absence check.

checks.title: Welcome series is live
checks.question: Does every new subscriber get a welcome series?
checks.why_it_matters: New subscribers are the most likely to buy, and the welcome series is where most first orders from email come from.
checks.logic: Apply conventions.flow_classifier for type welcome. Pass if >= 1 live welcome flow with >= 3 live email messages and recipients > 0 in the last 90 days. Warn if live but 1-2 messages, or zero recipients in 90 days. Fail if none.

thresholds.warn: 1-2 emails, or live with zero 90d recipients

impact.method: Monthly new email subscribers (CAP-02) x (target welcome revenue per subscriber - current) x 12.

checks.fix: Build a 3-5 email welcome: offer delivery immediately, brand/why-us, best sellers/social proof, offer reminder before expiry; exit on Placed Order; split buyers vs non-buyers.
checks.notes: Presence plus depth. See conventions.flow_classifier.

checks.title: Abandoned checkout flow is live
checks.question: Does everyone who starts checkout and doesn't buy get a recovery sequence?
checks.why_it_matters: People who reached checkout were seconds from buying; this is usually the highest-earning flow per email.
checks.logic: Apply the flow classifier for abandoned_checkout on the canonical checkout metric (DAT-02). Coverage = 90-day flow recipients / 90-day started_checkout uniques. Pass if live with >= 2 emails and coverage >= 25%. Warn if 1 email, or coverage 10-25%. Fail if no live flow, or coverage < 10%.

thresholds.pass: live, >= 2 emails, coverage >= 25% of checkout starters

impact.method: Monthly started_checkout uniques x identifiable share x (target recovery RPR - current) x 12.

checks.fix: Build 3 emails (1h, 24h, 72h) on the canonical Started Checkout metric with dynamic cart blocks; exit on Placed Order since flow start; add SMS step where consented.
checks.notes: Coverage is bounded by how many checkout starters Klaviyo can identify; a low ratio may be identification, not flow logic.

checks.title: Abandoned cart flow is live
checks.question: Do shoppers who add to cart but don't start checkout get a reminder?
checks.why_it_matters: Add-to-cart is a strong buying signal that reaches many more shoppers than checkout recovery alone.
checks.logic: Apply the flow classifier for abandoned_cart. Check it excludes people who started checkout (profile_filter profile-metric on checkout metric == 0 since flow start, or a trigger split) so it doesn't double up with FLW-02. Pass if live, >= 2 emails, and checkout starters excluded. Warn if live without checkout exclusion, or 1 email. Fail if none.

impact.method: Monthly added_to_cart uniques not starting checkout x identifiable share x target cart RPR x 12.

checks.fix: Build 2 emails (2-4h, 24h) on Added to Cart, filtered to no Started Checkout and no Placed Order since flow start, with smart sending on.
checks.notes: Requires an onsite Added to Cart event (DAT-02).

checks.title: Browse abandonment flow is live
checks.question: Do identified visitors who view products without adding to cart get a follow-up?
checks.why_it_matters: Browse abandonment turns high-volume product views into sales at very low cost.
checks.logic: Apply the flow classifier for browse. Check re-entry is limited (reentry_criteria or profile-not-in-flow filter >= 7 days) and that cart/checkout starters are excluded. Pass if live with >= 1 email, exclusions and re-entry limit. Warn if missing exclusions or re-entry limit. Fail if none.

thresholds.pass: live, exclusions and re-entry limit present
thresholds.warn: live without exclusions or re-entry limit

impact.method: Monthly viewed_product uniques x identifiable share x target browse RPR x 12.

checks.fix: Build 1-2 emails on Viewed Product with a dynamic product block, exclude cart/checkout/order since flow start, limit re-entry to once per 14 days.

checks.title: Post-purchase flow is live
checks.question: Do first-time buyers get a post-purchase sequence that builds toward a second order?
checks.why_it_matters: The weeks after the first order decide whether a buyer becomes a repeat customer.

source.path: 24: triggers[0].id -> metric 'Placed Order'/'Fulfilled Order' (canonical, DAT-01); flows.details[].definition.actions[] (time-delay data.{unit,value}; conditional-split data.profile_filter); 34: flow90 recipients

checks.logic: Apply the flow classifier for post_purchase. Check for a first-vs-repeat split (conditional-split on Placed Order count). Pass if live, >= 2 emails, and first-time buyers get a distinct path. Warn if live but one path for all buyers, or only 1 email. Fail if none.

impact.method: Monthly first-time buyers (RET-01) x (target 2nd-order rate lift) x average second-order value x 12; do not double count with RET-02.

checks.fix: Build thank-you/onboarding, how-to-use, review request, and cross-sell emails, with a first-time buyer branch and timing tied to delivery.
checks.notes: Shipping/transactional notifications from the store platform are not counted.

checks.title: Winback flow is live
checks.question: Do customers who have gone quiet past their normal reorder window get a winback sequence?
checks.why_it_matters: Lapsed customers already know the brand; a winback brings some back before they're lost for good.
checks.logic: Apply the flow classifier for winback (Placed Order trigger with first send >= 45 days, or segment trigger on lapsed buyers). Size the lapsed pool from placed-orders: pseudonymous buyers whose last order is between 1.5x and 4x the median repeat gap (RET-02) ago. Pass if live, sending, first send within 1.5-2x the median repeat gap. Warn if live but timed outside that window, or only 1 email. Fail if none.

thresholds.pass: live, sending, timed to 1.5-2x median repeat gap

impact.method: Lapsed pool x consented share (DAT-07) x target reactivation rate x AOV, annualised.

checks.fix: Build a 3-email winback triggered on Placed Order with delay at ~1.5x the median gap (exit on order), escalating from reminder to incentive; mirror for subscription cancels in RET-04.
checks.notes: Placed-orders covers 24 months only: 'first observed' is not 'truly new'.

checks.title: Sunset flow suppresses unengaged profiles
checks.question: Are long-unengaged subscribers given a last chance and then suppressed?
checks.why_it_matters: Mailing people who never open hurts inbox placement for everyone else on the list.
checks.logic: Find a live flow triggered by a segment whose definition uses no open/click/active-on-site in >= 90 days, ending in a suppression/update-profile action or list removal. Pass if live with a suppression step. Warn if a sunset segment exists and campaigns exclude it (CMP-03) but no flow. Fail if neither.

thresholds.pass: live sunset flow with suppression step
thresholds.warn: unengaged segment excluded from campaigns, no flow

impact.method: Indirect: protects deliverability (DLV-01..04); size as risk, not revenue.

checks.fix: Create an unengaged segment (no open/click 120-180d, subscribed > 120d, no order 180d), a 2-email re-permission flow, then suppress non-responders.
checks.notes: Opens are inflated by Apple Mail Privacy Protection; define engagement with clicks/site activity where possible.

checks.title: Flows earn a healthy share of email revenue
checks.question: What share of email-attributed revenue comes from automated flows rather than campaigns?
checks.why_it_matters: Flow revenue is earned without weekly effort; a low share usually means missing or broken automations.
checks.logic: Flow share = sum(flow conversion_value) / (sum(flow) + sum(campaign conversion_value)) for 365 and 90 days. Pass if >= 35%. Warn if 20-35%. Fail if < 20%. Also flag if 90-day share is > 10 points below 365-day share.

impact.method: Summary of FLW-01..07 gaps; do not add separately.

checks.fix: Repair the failing FLW presence checks first, in order of sized impact.
checks.notes: Step 34 currently returns email-channel rows only.

checks.title: Flows stop when the customer buys
checks.question: Do welcome, browse, cart and checkout flows exit people who place an order?
checks.why_it_matters: Sending 'you forgot something' after someone has bought looks careless and drives unsubscribes.

source.path: flows.details[].definition.profile_filter.condition_groups[].conditions[] where type == 'profile-metric' && metric_id == canonical Placed Order && measurement_filter.{operator:'equals',value:0} && timeframe_filter.operator == 'flow-start'; or conditional-split actions[].data.profile_filter with the same condition before each send

checks.logic: For each live welcome/browse/cart/checkout flow, check for a flow-level purchase exit on the canonical Placed Order metric (DAT-01), or a pre-send split with the same rule before every send. Pass if all have it. Warn if the exit uses a non-canonical order metric, or only some sends are guarded. Fail if any live abandonment flow has no purchase exit.

thresholds.pass: all live intent flows exit on canonical purchase
thresholds.fail: >= 1 live abandonment flow without purchase exit

impact.method: Not sized as revenue; reported as customer-experience and unsubscribe risk.

checks.fix: Add the flow filter 'Placed Order (canonical) zero times since starting this flow'; for welcome, branch buyers to a non-promotional path.
checks.notes: Presence/absence check.

checks.title: Flow guardrails are set
checks.question: Do marketing flow emails use smart sending, avoid the transactional flag, and contain no draft messages in live core flows?
checks.why_it_matters: Missing guardrails either over-mail customers or silently skip messages they should receive.

source.path: 24: flows.details[].definition.actions[].data.message.{smart_sending_enabled,transactional}, actions[].data.status, definition.reentry_criteria; 34: flow90 results[].statistics.recipients by flow_message_id

checks.logic: Across live core flows: (a) share of marketing send-email actions with smart_sending_enabled true (checkout/cart first email may be exempt); (b) any marketing message with transactional true; (c) send actions with data.status != 'live' inside live flows; (d) live messages with zero 90-day recipients. Pass if (a) >= 90%, (b)=0, (c)=0. Warn if (a) 70-90% or (c)/(d) > 0. Fail if (b) > 0 or (a) < 70%.

thresholds.pass: >= 90% smart sending; no transactional marketing; no drafts
thresholds.fail: marketing message flagged transactional, or < 70% smart sending

impact.method: Not sized; compliance and frequency risk.

checks.fix: Turn on smart sending for marketing flow emails, remove the transactional flag from promotional messages, and set draft messages live or remove them.

checks.title: Campaign cadence is steady
checks.question: How many email campaigns are sent per week, and is the rhythm consistent?
checks.why_it_matters: Too few sends leaves revenue on the table; erratic sends train subscribers to ignore you.
checks.logic: Count campaigns with status 'Sent' per ISO week in account timezone over the last 13 full weeks (deduplicate A/B and multi-audience splits by send date and name stem). Pass if average >= 2/week and no week is empty. Warn if 1-2/week, or >= 2 empty weeks. Fail if < 1/week.

impact.method: (Target sends/week - current) x 52 x median campaign revenue per send (step 34 campaign90), discounted 30% for fatigue.

checks.fix: Publish a 2-3 sends/week calendar (one promo, one content/product story, one segment-specific), engaged-segment first.
checks.notes: Over-sending is caught by DLV-01/03; deep track can add per-profile exposure from v2/exposure-sample.

checks.title: Campaign revenue per recipient is holding up
checks.question: Is campaign revenue per recipient in the last 90 days in line with the last year?
checks.why_it_matters: Falling revenue per email means campaigns are reaching less interested people or saying less compelling things.
checks.logic: Recipient-weighted RPR = sum(conversion_value) / sum(recipients) for 90 and 365 days. Ratio = RPR90 / RPR365. Pass if ratio >= 0.85. Warn if 0.6-0.85. Fail if < 0.6. Note seasonality when the 90-day window contains or excludes November-December.

impact.method: (RPR365 - RPR90) x annualised campaign recipients.

checks.fix: Shift sends to engaged segments (CMP-03), test offers and subject lines, and cut sends with RPR below 25% of median.
checks.notes: No absolute RPR benchmark until 5+ audits; compare within account.

checks.title: Campaigns target engaged segments
checks.question: Do campaigns go to engagement-based segments and exclude unengaged or suppressed groups, rather than the whole list?
checks.why_it_matters: Sending to everyone drags down inbox placement and wastes sends on people who never open.
checks.logic: For Sent campaigns in the last 90 days, classify each included ID as list or segment and whether the segment uses engagement conditions. Pass if >= 80% of sends include an engagement segment or exclude an unengaged segment. Warn if 50-80%. Fail if < 50% (mostly whole-list sends).

impact.method: Indirect via DLV-01..04 and CMP-02; size only if a deliverability check fails.

checks.fix: Create 30/60/90/180-day engaged segments (click or site activity based), default campaigns to 90-day engaged, expand only for major promos with an unengaged exclusion.
checks.notes: groupCounts sizes are membership counts, not reach (DAT-07).

checks.title: Campaign settings honour unsubscribes and frequency
checks.question: Are any campaigns set to ignore unsubscribes, and is smart sending used on promotional sends?
checks.why_it_matters: Mailing unsubscribed people is a compliance risk; no frequency control over-mails the best customers.
checks.logic: For Sent campaigns in the last 365 days: count ignore_unsubscribes == true and share with use_smart_sending == true. Pass if zero ignore_unsubscribes and smart sending >= 70%. Warn if smart sending < 70%. Fail if any ignore_unsubscribes on a non-transactional send.

thresholds.fail: any ignore_unsubscribes on a marketing send

impact.method: Not sized; compliance risk.

checks.fix: Turn off 'ignore unsubscribes' on all marketing campaigns, default smart sending on, and document the rare exceptions.

checks.title: Peak-season plan beats last year's baseline
checks.question: How did the last two November-December seasons perform, and does this year's plan improve on them?
checks.why_it_matters: Peak season is often a quarter of the year's revenue; repeating last year's gaps is the costliest mistake.
checks.logic: Compute per season: attributed share of Nov-Dec revenue, campaign count, and BFCM-week revenue share. Pass if the current plan has a dated calendar with >= last season's send count to engaged segments, pre-BFCM list-warming, and flows reviewed. Warn if last season's attributed share fell vs the season before with no plan change. Fail if no plan exists by mid-October.

thresholds.pass: dated plan >= last season, warming and flow review

impact.method: Last season attributed revenue x target lift in attributed share, conditional on DLV and CAP passing.

checks.fix: Build a dated Oct-Dec calendar: warm-up sends, early access, BFCM sequence, shipping cutoffs, and post-holiday replenishment/winback.
checks.notes: Plan existence is a human input; the baseline is collector data.

checks.title: Spam complaint rate is low
checks.question: What share of delivered emails are marked as spam, by month and by campaign?
checks.why_it_matters: Spam complaints are the fastest way to get the brand's email sent to junk at Gmail and Yahoo.
checks.logic: Monthly spam rate = marked_spam / received_email for each full month; also per-campaign spam_complaint_rate in the last 90 days. Pass if every month < 0.08% and no campaign >= 0.3%. Warn if any month 0.08-0.3%, or any campaign >= 0.3%. Fail if any month >= 0.3%.

impact.method: Risk, not revenue: share of email revenue exposed to inbox filtering.

checks.fix: Tighten campaign audiences (CMP-03), launch sunset (FLW-07), check list sources and consent wording, and make unsubscribe prominent.
checks.notes: 0.3% matches mailbox-provider bulk-sender guidance; Klaviyo only sees feedback-loop complaints, so Gmail complaints are under-counted (Postmaster Tools is manual).

checks.title: Bounce rate is low
checks.question: What share of sends bounce, how many are hard bounces, and how many are dropped as already suppressed?
checks.why_it_matters: High bounces signal an old or bought list and damage the sender's reputation.
checks.logic: Monthly bounce rate = bounced / (received + bounced); hard-bounce rate separately; dropped share = dropped / (received + dropped). Pass if bounce < 1% and hard < 0.3% every month. Warn if bounce 1-2% or any single campaign > 3%. Fail if any month > 2% or hard > 0.5%.

impact.method: Risk, not revenue.

checks.fix: Find the list sources behind bounce spikes, validate imports before sending, and confirm hard bounces are suppressed.

checks.title: Unsubscribe rate is in a normal range
checks.question: What share of delivered emails lead to an unsubscribe, by month and per campaign?
checks.why_it_matters: Rising unsubscribes mean we are sending too often or saying the wrong things to the wrong people.
checks.logic: Monthly rate = unsubscribed_email / received_email; per-campaign unsubscribe_rate (last 90 days). Pass if every month < 0.3% and < 10% of campaigns exceed 0.5%. Warn if a month is 0.3-0.6% or 10-25% of campaigns exceed 0.5%. Fail if any month > 0.6%.

impact.method: Excess unsubscribes x average annual revenue per subscriber.

checks.fix: Cap frequency for less-engaged tiers, add a preference centre with a 'send less' option, and audit high-unsubscribe campaigns.
checks.notes: Account-wide unsubscribes include flows and list-removal events; read with per-message rates.

checks.title: No inbox provider is falling behind
checks.question: Do Gmail, Microsoft, Yahoo and Apple recipients engage at similar rates?
checks.why_it_matters: A provider with much lower engagement usually means mail is landing in that provider's junk folder.
checks.logic: For providers with >= 2% of received volume over the last 3 full months, open rate = opened / received. Exclude Apple from the comparison base (Mail Privacy Protection auto-opens). Pass if every major non-Apple provider is >= 70% of the non-Apple weighted average. Warn if one is 50-70%. Fail if any major provider is < 50% or fell > 30% month over month.

impact.method: Revenue at risk = share of received volume at the lagging provider x email-attributed revenue x estimated junk share.

checks.fix: Run a provider-specific warm-up to engaged recipients, check Postmaster/SNDS manually, and confirm authentication (DLV-05/06).
checks.notes: Opens are a weak signal; clicks by provider are not collected (a click_by_inbox aggregate would strengthen this).

checks.title: Mail sends from a branded, authenticated domain
checks.question: Is a dedicated branded sending domain verified, with SPF, DKIM and a DMARC policy published?
checks.why_it_matters: Gmail and Yahoo now require authenticated, aligned mail from bulk senders, or they filter it.

source.path: today: q4-baseline.json sendingDomains.{ok:false} (404 in all saved snapshots); fallback evidence: account-audit-api.json flows.details[].definition.actions[].data.message.from_email domain and account-totals.json campaigns.email.messages[].attributes.definition.content.from_email domain vs account.contact.website_url; analyst/dns/<slug>.txt (ad hoc dig output)

checks.logic: Pass if Klaviyo reports a verified branded sending domain, DKIM CNAMEs resolve, SPF is valid, and _dmarc has p=quarantine or p=reject with an rua address. Warn if DMARC is p=none, or from_email domains are inconsistent across messages. Fail if no branded sending domain (shared Klaviyo domain) or no DMARC record.

thresholds.pass: verified branded domain; SPF+DKIM; DMARC quarantine/reject
thresholds.warn: DMARC p=none, or mixed from domains
thresholds.fail: no branded domain or no DMARC

impact.method: Risk, not revenue.

checks.fix: Set up the branded sending subdomain in Klaviyo, publish the DKIM/SPF records it gives, publish DMARC at p=none with reporting, then move to quarantine after 2-4 clean weeks.
checks.notes: Step 35's /sending-domains call returns 404 for all four saved accounts; a DNS step (dig) should write structured output instead of the ad hoc text files. DNS alone does not prove aligned live mail (see DLV-06).

checks.title: Live mail is DMARC-aligned in received headers
checks.question: Do real received campaign and flow emails pass SPF/DKIM with alignment to the From domain?
checks.why_it_matters: DNS records can look right while live mail still fails alignment; only a received message proves it.

source.path: Authentication-Results and DKIM-Signature headers from a seed inbox (Gmail + Outlook) for one campaign and one flow email; record d=, smtp.mailfrom, dmarc=pass/fail

checks.logic: Pass if dmarc=pass with aligned DKIM d= domain (organizational match to From) on both providers. Warn if pass via SPF alignment only. Fail if dmarc=fail or DKIM signed only by a shared Klaviyo domain.

thresholds.pass: dmarc=pass with aligned DKIM at both providers

impact.method: Risk, not revenue.

checks.fix: Complete branded sending-domain setup (DLV-05) and re-test with a seed send.
checks.notes: Presence/absence check on received evidence. Gate for audience expansion.

checks.title: First-time buyers come back
checks.question: What share of first-time buyers place a second order within 12 months?
checks.why_it_matters: Repeat customers are the cheapest revenue; a low repeat rate caps growth no matter how many new buyers arrive.

source.path: orders[].{p (pseudonymous profile id),t,v,o}; truncated, start, end

checks.logic: Deduplicate orders by o. Cohort = profiles whose first observed order falls between 24 and 12 months before capture (so each has 12 months of follow-up). Repeat rate = share with >= 2 orders within 365 days of the first. Pass if >= 25%. Warn if 15-25%. Fail if < 15%. Report by first-order month to show trend.

impact.method: Annual first-time buyers x (target repeat rate - current) x average second-order value; shared pool with FLW-05/RET-02, count once.

checks.fix: Fix FLW-05 post-purchase and RET-02 timing first; then add a second-purchase incentive and product-education content.
checks.notes: First observed in a 24-month window is not truly new; null p rows are excluded and counted. Vertical norms vary widely; calibrate after 5+ audits.

checks.title: Follow-up timing matches when customers reorder
checks.question: Does the post-purchase or replenishment flow reach buyers before their typical reorder date?
checks.why_it_matters: A reminder that arrives after the customer has already run out, or bought elsewhere, earns little.

source.path: 38: orders[].{p,t,i}; 24: flows.details[] with Placed Order trigger -> definition.actions[] type 'time-delay' data.{unit,value} cumulative to each send-email

checks.logic: Median and 25th percentile days between 1st and 2nd order (by product family when DAT-03 passes). Cumulative delay to each post-purchase/replenishment email. Pass if a live email lands between the 25th percentile and the median gap. Warn if the closest email is within 0.5-1.5x the median but outside that band. Fail if no email lands before 1.5x the median gap.

thresholds.pass: an email lands between p25 and median reorder gap

impact.method: Buyers reaching the reorder window per month x consented share x target reorder lift x AOV x 12.

checks.fix: Add a replenishment branch timed at ~p25 of the gap (per product when line items exist), with a reorder link and subscription offer.
checks.notes: Product-level timing needs line items (DAT-03); otherwise use account-level gap.

checks.title: Subscription events are flowing
checks.question: If the brand sells subscriptions, are the subscription platform's events (started, cancelled, paused, renewal) reaching Klaviyo?
checks.why_it_matters: Without subscription events we can't save cancellations or remind subscribers before renewal.
checks.logic: n/a if no subscription product (client-confirmed). Otherwise list subscription metrics; require started/created, cancelled (or status change) and renewal/charge events. Pass if all three types have events in each of the last 2 full months. Warn if one type is missing or a month is zero. Fail if subscription is sold but no subscription metric has events in the last 2 full months.

thresholds.pass: start, cancel and renewal events each month
thresholds.warn: one type missing or a zero month

impact.method: Not sized directly; enables RET-04.

checks.fix: Reconnect the subscription app's Klaviyo integration (Loop, Recharge, WooCommerce Subscriptions), confirm event names, and fire a test event.
checks.notes: Keep the native subscription platform's own service messages; avoid counting one order as a campaign win, refill win and save.

checks.title: Subscription lifecycle flows are live
checks.question: Are there live flows for subscription cancellation, pause, failed payment and upcoming renewal?
checks.why_it_matters: Saving even a small share of cancelling subscribers protects the most predictable revenue the brand has.

source.path: 24: flows.details[].definition.triggers[0].id in subscription metric IDs (metricChoices.subscription_*), flows.items[].attributes.status; 38: aggregates.subscription_* counts for sizing

checks.logic: n/a if RET-03 is n/a. Map live flows to subscription metrics: cancelled, paused, failed payment, upcoming charge. Pass if cancellation and upcoming-renewal flows are live (or confirmed handled natively in the subscription app). Warn if only one is covered. Fail if neither.

impact.method: Monthly cancellations x target save rate x average subscription value x expected remaining months.

checks.fix: Build a cancellation winback (reason-based), pre-renewal reminder with swap/skip options, and failed-payment recovery; coordinate with the app's native notices to avoid duplicates.
checks.notes: Native app messaging counts as coverage only with client confirmation (manual).

checks.title: Emails stay under Gmail's clipping limit
checks.question: Are any live flow or recent campaign emails larger than about 102 KB of HTML, so Gmail cuts them off?
checks.why_it_matters: Gmail hides everything after the cut, including the unsubscribe link and often the main offer.

source.path: 37: templates[].{htmlBytes,overGmailClipThreshold,messages[].flowId}, overGmailClipThreshold, uniqueLiveTemplates, errors; 40: email-archive/klaviyo-campaigns.json campaigns[].html_file -> byte length

checks.logic: Count live flow templates with htmlBytes > 102,400 (step 37's rule). Deep: also measure the last 90 days of campaign HTML from step 40. Pass if none clip. Warn if any template is 90-102 KB, or clipping is only in low-volume messages. Fail if any core-flow message or > 10% of recent campaigns clip.

thresholds.warn: templates 90-102 KB, or clipping in low-volume messages
thresholds.fail: core-flow message or > 10% of recent campaigns clip

impact.method: Not sized; reported as render and compliance risk on affected messages' recipients.

checks.fix: Remove inline-style bloat and hidden blocks, shorten long product grids, and re-measure until under 90 KB.
checks.notes: Step 37 covers live flow templates only; campaign coverage needs the deep step 40 archive. Template HTML is not a received message.

checks.title: Emails are not image-only
checks.question: Do live emails carry real HTML text, or are they mostly images?
checks.why_it_matters: Image-only emails look blank when images are blocked, can't be read by screen readers, and filter worse.
checks.logic: Flag templates with textChars < 300 and imageCount >= 3 as image-heavy. Pass if < 10% of live templates are image-heavy and no core-flow first email is. Warn if 10-30%. Fail if > 30%, or the welcome/checkout first email is image-heavy.

thresholds.fail: > 30%, or a core first email image-heavy

impact.method: Not sized.

checks.fix: Rebuild headlines, offers and CTAs as live text with alt text on every image; keep images for product and lifestyle only.
checks.notes: Deep track: confirm mobile legibility and dark mode on step 29 renders.

checks.title: Links go to the live store
checks.question: Do every link in live flow and recent campaign emails resolve to a working page on the current domain?
checks.why_it_matters: A broken or old-domain link sends a ready buyer to an error page.

source.path: inputs already saved: flow-email-renders/*.html (step 29), email-archive/html/*.html (step 40); live website from account.contact.website_url

checks.logic: Extract unique hrefs (resolve Klaviyo tracking wrappers), request each, record final URL and status. Pass if 100% resolve 2xx on the current domain. Warn if any redirect chains > 2 hops or land on a generic page. Fail if any link 4xx/5xx or points at an old/foreign domain in a core flow.

thresholds.warn: long redirect chains or generic landing
thresholds.fail: any 4xx/5xx or old-domain link in core flows

impact.method: Recipients of messages with broken primary CTA x message RPR (step 34).

checks.fix: Update links in the template or universal blocks, replace hard-coded old domains, and re-run the check.
checks.notes: Lesson from a past audit: emails still carried links to a retired domain.

checks.title: Clicks are tracked with UTMs
checks.question: Do flow and campaign emails add tracking parameters so site analytics can attribute email traffic?
checks.why_it_matters: Without UTMs the client's analytics undercounts email, which weakens the case for investing in it.
checks.logic: Share of live flow send-email actions and last-90-day campaigns with add_tracking_params true. Pass if >= 90% of both. Warn if 50-90%. Fail if < 50%, or click tracking is off on any campaign.

impact.method: Not sized.

checks.fix: Enable account-level UTM tracking with a consistent source/medium/campaign scheme and turn it on per flow message.

checks.title: Promised offers work at checkout
checks.question: Does every offer promised in forms and emails apply correctly at checkout, at the stated value, without unintended stacking?
checks.why_it_matters: An offer that fails at checkout breaks trust at the exact moment someone is trying to buy.

source.path: offer copy: form-details.json html_text components (step 31) and welcome/flow message copy (account-audit-api.json flows.details[].actions[].messages[].bodyText); codes in use: placed-orders-24mo.json orders[].d (Shopify only); checkout test evidence recorded by the auditor

checks.logic: List each promised offer (value, expiry, exclusions). Test at checkout: code applies, value matches copy, stacking with sitewide/subscription discounts behaves as intended, expiry is real. Pass if all match. Warn if copy omits material exclusions. Fail if any promised code fails or stacks beyond the intended total.

thresholds.fail: any promised offer fails or stacks unexpectedly

impact.method: Margin leakage from unintended stacking (orders with stacked codes x excess discount) plus lost conversions on failed codes.

checks.fix: Align copy to the actual discount rules, set combinability in the store, and use unique expiring codes for welcome offers.
checks.notes: Sequential discounts compound (25% then 15% is 36.25%, not 40%). Coupons/catalog in step 38 returned 0 items for all saved accounts, so codes cannot be read from Klaviyo today.

checks.title: Forms collect SMS consent
checks.question: Do live sign-up forms collect a phone number with compliant SMS consent?
checks.why_it_matters: SMS is often the highest-converting channel, but only if consent is collected at sign-up.
checks.logic: n/a if the brand does not run SMS. Pass if the primary live popup has a phone step with SMS consent (consent type recorded) after email capture. Warn if only secondary forms collect phone. Fail if SMS is run but no live form collects consent.

thresholds.fail: SMS run, no form collects consent

impact.method: Primary form submits x target phone opt-in rate x SMS revenue per subscriber.

checks.fix: Add a second step for phone with TCPA-compliant consent language; if SMS runs on a third-party platform, use its form or a sync (SMS-05).
checks.notes: Presence/absence check.

checks.title: Klaviyo SMS messages meet compliance settings
checks.question: Do Klaviyo flow SMS messages include opt-out language, brand identification and quiet hours?
checks.why_it_matters: Missing opt-out language or texting at night risks carrier filtering and legal exposure.
checks.logic: n/a if there are no send-sms actions. For live SMS actions: Pass if all have opt-out language (or it is in the body), org prefix, and quiet hours. Warn if any lack org prefix. Fail if any lack opt-out language or quiet hours.

impact.method: Not sized; compliance risk.

checks.fix: Enable opt-out language, brand prefix and quiet hours on each SMS message; review the first message in each flow for consent context.
checks.notes: Campaign SMS settings are not in step 24; step 38 campaigns.sms.items[] has send options for SMS campaigns.

checks.title: SMS opt-out and failure rates are low
checks.question: What share of delivered texts lead to an opt-out, and how many fail to deliver?
checks.why_it_matters: High opt-outs burn an expensive list; high failures waste spend and can signal carrier filtering.

source.path: metricChoices.{received_sms,unsubscribed_sms,failed_sms,clicked_sms}.used (null = not on Klaviyo SMS), aggregates.received_sms / unsubscribed_sms / failed_sms .current.rows[0].measurements.count[]

checks.logic: n/a if received_sms.used is null. Monthly opt-out rate = unsubscribed_sms / received_sms; failure rate = failed / (received + failed). Pass if opt-out < 1.5% and failure < 3% every month. Warn if opt-out 1.5-3% or failure 3-6%. Fail if opt-out > 3% or failure > 6%.

impact.method: Excess opt-outs x SMS revenue per subscriber.

checks.fix: Reduce SMS frequency for non-buyers, target SMS campaigns to recent clickers/buyers, and clean numbers that fail repeatedly.
checks.notes: Metric names vary (SMS vs Text Message); step 38 metric-selection.js handles the aliases.

checks.title: SMS earns a measurable share of revenue
checks.question: How much revenue does SMS drive, and is it measured per message?
checks.why_it_matters: SMS costs money per message, so it must show clear revenue to justify itself.

source.path: aggregates.placed_order_by_channel.current.rows[] where dimensions[0] == '$sms_channel' -> measurements.sum_value[]; campaigns.sms.{count,items[]}; per-message SMS performance not collected (step 34 results[].groupings.send_channel is 'email' only)

checks.logic: n/a if no Klaviyo SMS. SMS share = $sms_channel value / (email + SMS attributed value). Pass if SMS sends exist and SMS has attributed revenue in each of the last 3 months. Warn if SMS sends exist but attributed revenue is zero or missing in any month (check DAT-06 first). Fail if SMS sends exist and no SMS revenue appears in the window.

thresholds.pass: SMS revenue every month with sends
thresholds.fail: sends with no measured SMS revenue

impact.method: Not sized until per-message SMS cost and revenue are collected.

checks.fix: Confirm SMS attribution settings, then add an SMS-filtered step 34 report so each SMS message's revenue and cost can be judged.
checks.notes: Channel-level only. Per-message SMS revenue needs step 34 to request send_channel 'sms' (collector gap). In saved snapshots only '$email_channel' appears even where SMS campaigns exist; investigate before reporting SMS as zero.

checks.title: Third-party SMS platform is reconciled
checks.question: If SMS runs outside Klaviyo, are consent, suppressions and journeys synced so customers aren't double-messaged or messaged after opting out?
checks.why_it_matters: Two disconnected platforms can text and email the same person the same reminder, or keep texting after opt-out.

source.path: evidence hints: account-audit-api.json metrics.items[].attributes.integration.name (e.g. third-party SMS/subscription apps); platform admin screens for consent sync, opt-out sync and active journeys

checks.logic: n/a if all SMS runs in Klaviyo or there is no SMS. Pass if consent and opt-outs sync both ways, overlapping journeys (welcome, cart, checkout) are coordinated, and SMS revenue is reported from the SMS platform. Warn if sync is one-way. Fail if no sync or overlapping journeys fire on both platforms uncoordinated.

thresholds.fail: no sync or uncoordinated duplicate journeys

impact.method: Not sized in the audit; migration or consolidation is a separate scoped decision.

checks.fix: Enable the platform's Klaviyo integration for consent and events, assign each journey to one channel owner, and add cross-channel exclusions.
checks.notes: Client approves any SMS cutover; do not treat historical buyers as SMS-consented.
